about.title: Stockton Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Stockton walk into a clinic or hospital expecting to leave better than they arrived. When a missed diagnosis, a surgical error, or a medication mix-up sends things the other way, the shock is usually followed by a harder question: was this simply a bad result, or did someone fall short of the standard of care? California law draws that line carefully. A poor outcome by itself is not malpractice; there has to be a departure from what a reasonably careful provider would have done, and a qualified medical expert almost always has to say so. Timing matters too. Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, with a 90-day notice sent to the provider before any lawsuit is filed. We handle San Joaquin County medical malpractice cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: MICRA deadlines get tracked from day one
items.desc: The one-year discovery window and three-year outer limit can close faster than people expect. Our team will work out which dates apply to you and handle the required 90-day pre-suit notice.

items.title: Expert review, not guesswork
items.desc: California cases almost always require a qualified medical expert to explain how the care fell short. We know how to line that up and can tell you honestly if a bad outcome doesn't rise to malpractice.

items.title: No fee unless there's a recovery
items.desc: Malpractice cases are expensive to build, so we work on contingency. You also get a straight explanation of how California's non-economic damages cap, which rises each year, may apply to your situation.

items.question: I was treated at a Stockton emergency room after a crash on Hammer Lane and they missed a fracture. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but the answer depends on what a reasonably careful ER provider would have done with the same symptoms and imaging. Stockton logged 1,313 injury collisions in 2025, and crash patients are common in local emergency rooms, so a missed injury after a wreck is something we see. A qualified medical expert would need to review the records and say whether the miss was a departure from the standard of care. Note that you may also have a separate claim tied to the crash itself.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and in no event more than three years from when the injury occurred. There are some exceptions, such as for minors or when a foreign object is left in the body. Before filing suit, a 90-day notice must go to the provider. Because these rules interact, it's worth talking to us as early as you can.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a malpractice case?
items.answer: California's MICRA law places a cap on non-economic damages, meaning things like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. That cap now increases every year under the current statute. Economic losses such as medical bills and lost income are not subject to the same cap. We can explain how the current figures would apply to your specific circumstances.
